name: WBI Energy Bakken East Pipeline
researcher_notes: Gas pipeline in North Dakota. WBI Energy Transmission proposes about 374 miles from near Watford City to its compressor station near Mapleton, built in two phases. The company project page says the length is about 374 miles after a binding open season in March 2026 and gives FERC pre-filing docket PF26-4. The EIA August 2026 release, Natural Gas Pipeline Projects sheet, Excel row 12, lists 350 miles, 1,000 million cubic feet per day, 36 or 42 inch for phase 1 and 24, 30 or 36 inch for phase 2, status pre-applied, in service 2029. The later 374 mile figure is used. Oil and Gas Watch (May 13, 2026) reports 374 miles, 1 billion cubic feet per day, state financing of up to 500 million dollars confirmed April 29, 2026, FERC scoping meetings, phase 1 in November 2029 and phase 2 in November 2030. FERC issued a notice of scoping in May 2026 per EIA. Concrete step met: FERC pre-filing, binding open season, state financing. Not an existing row. Not North Bakken Expansion (P3162), a different smaller system. Intensity Gas Pipeline (P7782 and P7783) is a rival project from a different sponsor, Intensity Infrastructure Partners, on a similar corridor. EIA lists the line as intrastate, so a FERC docket exists only because of the pre-filing. EIA also lists an extra lateral of about 90 miles from Jamestown to Ellendale, not included in the 374 miles on the company page. The EIA Tioga to Emerson Project (330 miles, on hold) is a separate older WBI proposal and was not researched here. Two EIA entries for this project are one project. No cost is stated in EIA or the sources, so none is staged. Parent company not sourced, left blank. Owner spelled in the team's style with the legal form; gazetteer only has 'WBI Energy', so confirm the entity. Route not found: no official map in the sources checked, route research not done. Diameter left blank because phases differ (36 or 42 inch; 24, 30 or 36 inch) and no single value is confirmed. Tier high for existence and length (operator page plus independent news report); capacity and dates from EIA and news.
